# Baseline comparison: Sifted and Stone Soup

<!-- Generated by sifted_montecarlo (eval/sifted_montecarlo.cpp) via benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup/compare.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Sifted against an independent tracker built from an established open-source framework (Stone Soup), on the same Monte Carlo runs and the same input files, scored by the same scorer (Stone Soup's tracks go through the track report interchange format, `eval/sifted/eval/track_report.hpp`). Pairing is by run (common random numbers). How the trackers are configured, and every place where they cannot be matched exactly, is in [benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup/README.md](../benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup/README.md) and ADR 0015. No tracker was tuned on these runs. The Sifted-only Monte Carlo evaluation, with more runs and the network condition, is [evaluation-monte-carlo.md](evaluation-monte-carlo.md). Processing time is machine dependent and so is not on this page: see [benchmarks/baseline-timing.md](benchmarks/baseline-timing.md).

## What was run

```bash
build/stonesoup-venv/bin/python benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup/compare.py
```

which runs `sifted_montecarlo --manifest MANIFEST --trackers sifted,sifted-cv,sifted-cv-fixed-q --tracks stonesoup=DIR --reference stonesoup --network none --page baseline` on the generated manifest. Base seed 20261119, 760 generated runs. Each run's sensor seeds derive from (base seed, scenario, run index) through SplitMix64 (`sim/sifted_sim/montecarlo.py`), the same in every condition. Scenarios: `close_pass`, `crossing_pair`, `demo`, `enter_leave`, `formation_split` (definitions in `sim/sifted_sim/scenarios.py`).

| tracker | what it is |
|---|---|
| sifted | Sifted, `EngineConfig` defaults: IMM estimator (ADR 0014), GNN, chi-square gate 0.999, 3-hit confirmation |
| sifted-cv | Sifted with the legacy constant-velocity filter (q = 4 m^2/s^3) and its manoeuvre process-noise switching (x10 on a fading-memory NIS test) |
| sifted-cv-fixed-q | Sifted, constant-velocity filter with fixed q = 4 m^2/s^3 (manoeuvre switching off): the like-for-like configuration for an EKF/CV baseline |
| stonesoup | Stone Soup 1.9.1 (Python 3.12.3, numpy 2.5.5, scipy 1.18.1): EKF (ExtendedKalmanPredictor/Updater, Joseph form), constant velocity q = 4 m^2/s^3, range-bearing and bearing-only updates, squared-Mahalanobis chi-square gate 0.999, global nearest neighbour (GNNWith2DAssignment), MultiMeasurementInitiator (3 hits, 3 s), deletion 10 s after the last range-bearing update or at position sigma > 1000 m; not tuned (benchmarks/baselines/stonesoup) |

## Targets never tracked

No target was left untracked in any run: every target that should have been tracked has an RMSE in every run.

## Method and metric definitions

- **Unit of analysis: the run.** Every interval is computed from one value per run (a run's RMSE, ID-switch count, GOSPA, ...), never from time samples within a run, which are strongly correlated.
- **Point estimates and intervals.** Mean over runs with a 95% seeded percentile bootstrap interval (2000 resamples, base seed 1; `eval/sifted/eval/stats.hpp`). Counts (ID switches, false tracks) are skewed, and the bootstrap makes no normality assumption. With no event in n runs it shows `0 [0, u]`: u = -ln(0.025)/n = 3.69/n is the exact Poisson 95% upper bound on the mean per run. Fractions of runs ("runs with an ID switch") use the Wilson score interval.
- **Paired comparisons** use common random numbers: run r of a scenario has the same sensor noise, detections and clutter in every condition and for every tracker, so the difference is taken run by run and the interval is the bootstrap of the mean difference. "No detectable difference" means the interval contains 0.
- **Scoring** is the scorecard's own (`eval/sifted/eval/scenario.hpp`, [evaluation.md](evaluation.md)): CLEAR-MOT style matching within 100 m. RMSE per target over covered, matched instants at least 10 s after the target enters coverage; a run's mean RMSE averages its tracked targets and its worst RMSE is its largest. Missed %: covered target-instants at least 5 s after entering coverage with no matched track. ID switch: a target matched to a different track than the last time it was matched. False track: a reported track matched to a target in fewer than half of the instants it was reported.
- **GOSPA** (alpha = 2; Rahmathullah, García-Fernández and Svensson, FUSION 2017, arXiv:1601.05585; `eval/sifted/eval/gospa.hpp`) with **c = 100 m, p = 2**, per truth instant from 5 s after the first, between the targets counted for "missed" and the reported (confirmed and coasting) tracks. A track matched to a target that is present but out of coverage or still in its burn-in is left out of both sets. c equals the matching distance, so a GOSPA miss or false track is what the CLEAR-MOT matcher would call one (sized at about 5x the filtered radar error at the 8 km edge of coverage and below the closest lane spacing, 120 m). p = 2 weighs localisation errors as RMSE does. A run's GOSPA is (mean over instants of d^p)^(1/p), the RMS GOSPA for p = 2. The decomposition splits the mean d^p into localisation (assigned pairs), missed targets and false tracks (c^p/2 each), exactly additive.
- **Never tracked**: target-runs where the target was covered past the RMSE burn-in but never matched. Their RMSE is undefined. They are counted here, not dropped silently, and the RMSE columns average only the runs and targets that have one.
- **TrackLimit**: measurements that could not start a track because the engine was at `max_tracks` (1024), summed over runs (runs with any). Not available (n/a) for external trackers.
- **Determinism.** The same binary on the same architecture, given the same manifest (scenario code and base seed), writes the same bytes. Different compilers or maths libraries may change the last bits of the simulated noise (Python `sin`/`cos`) or of the filters, and so individual runs. The intervals are meant to absorb exactly that kind of variation.
